claims.claim: Finite-sequence survival with unrotatable dominoes is in NP.
claims.evidence: For each explicitly listed domino, a certificate may give its locking anchor. With the current board fixed, all collision-free positions of that fixed orientation form an O(WH)-vertex directed translation graph. Breadth-first search verifies spawn-to-lock reachability; a reachable lock always has a simple polynomial-length path. Collision, downward support, loss, placement, and simultaneous row deletion are then checked directly before processing the next piece. This is polynomial in the explicit board and sequence sizes.
claims.witness: The locking-coordinate list ((x_i,y_i)) for all pieces is a polynomial-size certificate, with reachability recomputed rather than trusted.
claims.search_method: Independent verifier construction from the source movement and clearing rules; polynomial state-count analysis.

claims.claim: For row-parallel unrotatable dominoes on an odd-width board, there is a computable linear-size upper bound on the number of pieces that can ever survive.
claims.evidence: A horizontal domino remains within one physical row token. Before an initial token clears, its initially occupied cells permanently separate its empty intervals, so interval length l accepts at most floor(l/2) dominoes and an initial token can clear only when every such length is even. If C is the summed capacity and q counts tokens satisfying that necessary parity condition, at most q initial tokens clear. Every introduced empty odd-width token accepts at most m=floor(W/2) dominoes and cannot clear. Hence every play has length at most U=C+qm, with C<=Hm and qm<=Hm, so U<=H(W-1).
claims.witness: The computable certificate of the bound is the list of initial empty-interval lengths, yielding U=C+q floor(W/2).
claims.search_method: Independent row-token invariant proof plus exhaustive exact state search over 4,628 small initial-board/spawn cases.

claims.claim: On an odd-width board with arbitrary mixed fixed orientations, every survivable prefix obeys a computable horizontal-versus-vertical obstruction h <= C + m b(v) <= U + (W-1)v.
claims.evidence: For every clearing initial token, each initially odd empty interval requires a vertical endpoint; every clearing introduced odd-width token likewise requires one. These charges occupy distinct cells, so sum_{R in S}d(R)+z<=2v. If q>0 this gives s<=q+2v. If q=0, the first clear must be an initial token costing at least delta=min_R d(R), and every later clear costs at least one more endpoint, giving no clear for 2v<delta and otherwise s<=2v-delta+1. Initial tokens contain at most C horizontal dominoes and the s introduced tokens at most ms, proving h<=C+mb(v). The stated coarse inequality follows from b(v)<=q+2v and U=C+qm.
claims.witness: The injective charge from every required odd-interval parity defect to a locked vertical-domino endpoint establishes the clear-count bound.
claims.search_method: Independent parity-charge proof, including the q=0 startup case; exact exploration checked 78,968 reachable count-state nodes from 2,353 small initial/spawn cases.

claims.claim: The coefficient W-1 in the mixed odd-width obstruction is asymptotically sharp: on every initially empty odd W by H board with W>=3 and H>=3, the block consisting of one vertical domino followed by W-1 horizontal dominoes can be repeated indefinitely.
claims.evidence: Put the vertical domino in an outer column of the bottom two rows. The remaining W-1 bottom cells form an even interval tiled by m=(W-1)/2 horizontal dominoes; clearing that row leaves the vertical domino's upper endpoint in the bottom row. The same m placements clear that row and restore the empty board. Empty top corridors make every specified lock reachable for H>=3. Repetition has h/v=W-1, so any smaller universal coefficient with a fixed initial-board intercept eventually fails.
claims.witness: The exact cycle is V at column 1, followed by horizontal pairs (2,3),(4,5),...,(W-1,W), then the same horizontal pairs again.
claims.search_method: Independent constructive proof; exact reachability replayed two complete cycles for all 204 tested combinations of W in {3,5,7}, H in {3,4,5}, horizontal spawn edge, and vertical spawn column.

claims.claim: On an even-width board, two initially empty top rows suffice for survival of arbitrarily many row-parallel unrotatable dominoes.
claims.evidence: Partition the columns into adjacent pairs. Dropping one horizontal domino on a pair equalizes the two column tops unless a row clears first. With the top row retained as a travel corridor, raise every lower pair top to the greatest pair top T. If no earlier clear occurred, row T-1 becomes full. Any clear ends the phase; the previously empty top row shifts down and a new empty row enters, restoring two empty top rows. Each phase is finite, contains a placement, and can be repeated indefinitely.
claims.witness: The repeatable phase is pair equalization followed by raising all pair tops to their common maximum, stopping at the first clear.
claims.search_method: Independent invariant/reachability proof plus exact cycle reachability for 733 exhaustive small initial-board/spawn cases.

claims.claim: On any height-at-least-three board with no complete row and two empty top rows, every finite all-vertical unrotatable-domino sequence is survivable.
claims.evidence: Let h_c be one plus the highest occupied row in column c and T=max h_c. Raise each column by vertical dominoes to the least t_c>=T of the same parity as h_c. Then t_c is T or T+1 and at most H-1, while every column occupies row T-1, forcing a clear unless one occurred earlier. When a final lift reaches the second-highest row, performing corridor-blocking lifts farthest-to-nearest on each side of the spawn column, with that column last, preserves reachability. A clear restores two empty top rows. The empty-board case fills and clears the bottom two rows. Thus the phase repeats for arbitrarily many pieces.
claims.witness: The column target vector t_c=min{t>=T:t congruent to h_c mod 2} supplies a finite clearing phase; the empty board uses one bottom vertical domino per column.
claims.search_method: Independent column-parity and corridor-order proof plus exact reachable-cycle checks for 253 exhaustive small initial-board/spawn cases.

claims.claim: Two empty top rows do not suffice for arbitrary mixed orientations: on the empty 4×3 board with centered horizontal spawn, the fixed sequence VHHHH is not survivable, irrespective of the vertical spawn column.
claims.evidence: The vertical domino leaves one occupied cell in each of the bottom two rows. Each row consequently has only one available adjacent horizontal pair and cannot clear by horizontal placements because its occupancy remains odd. If the sequence is to continue, the first two horizontal dominoes must therefore use those two rows. The third horizontal domino locks in the top row. Every top-row horizontal edge of width four intersects the centered spawn pair in columns 2-3, while one domino does not fill the row, so the fourth horizontal domino cannot spawn.
claims.witness: The empty 4×3 board with sequence VHHHH is the concrete obstruction; all four possible vertical spawn columns were checked.
claims.search_method: Independent parity/capacity argument and exhaustive exact reachability for each vertical spawn column.

claims.claim: The maximum survival length on an initially empty odd-width W×H board with row-parallel unrotatable dominoes is exactly H floor(W/2).
claims.evidence: Every row begins with even occupancy and each horizontal placement adds two cells, so an odd-width row never fills and no clear occurs. Each of the H rows therefore contains at most floor(W/2) disjoint dominoes. Conversely, every edge of an odd path belongs to a maximum matching. Choose a maximum row matching containing the fixed spawn edge and fill rows bottom-up. On the top row, place edges farthest-to-nearest on each side and the spawn edge last. This preserves spawn access and realizes the upper bound. For W=1 both sides are zero.
claims.witness: A maximum matching of the W-cell row path containing the spawn edge, repeated on all H levels, realizes H floor(W/2) placements.
claims.search_method: Independent parity upper bound and constructive matching proof; exact maxima checked in 16 small dimension/spawn cases.

claims.claim: The row-capacity bound is not sufficient, and clearing one row does not guarantee indefinite unrotatable-domino survival.
claims.evidence: On .../.#./... in a 3×3 board, C=2 and q=0, but both possible horizontal positions meet the middle obstruction, so the first piece locks in the top row and blocks every next spawn; the true maximum is one. On the 3×2 board .../..#, filling the two remaining bottom cells clears that row and leaves an empty board. The empty odd-width board then accepts exactly two more horizontal dominoes, so this position clears a row yet survives only three pieces.
claims.witness: The two concrete boards are .../.#./... with maximum one despite U=2, and .../..# with a first-row clear but maximum three.
claims.search_method: Independent move enumeration and exact state-space verification for both witness families and both width-three spawn edges.

claims.claim: Two initially empty top rows cannot in general be weakened to one on even-width row-parallel boards.
claims.evidence: On the 4×2 board ..../#... with centered spawn, the first domino either blocks the next spawn by locking at top columns 1-2, or leaves the bottom row as ###. or #.##. In either latter state no adjacent bottom pair remains. The second domino must lock in the top row, where every horizontal edge intersects the centered spawn pair; it cannot fill the row and therefore blocks the third piece. The exact maximum is two.
claims.witness: The board top/bottom = ..../#... with centered horizontal spawn survives two pieces but not three.
claims.search_method: Independent enumeration of all first-lock cases and exact exhaustive reachability.

claims.claim: For odd-width row-parallel instances whose completely empty initial rows form a top prefix, finite clearing polynomial-time many-one reduces to finite survival.
claims.evidence: If a nonempty initial token has an odd empty interval, or the clearing sequence length differs from K0=sum c_i over nonempty tokens, clearing is impossible and a fixed NO instance may be output. Otherwise output the same board with L=K0+Hm horizontal pieces. A clearing play followed by the empty-board Hm construction survives L pieces. Conversely, the token bound equals L because top-prefix empty tokens contribute their capacities and the nonempty parity-compatible tokens are the only possible initial clears. Saturating L therefore forces every nonempty initial token to clear. Empty-origin and introduced tokens always remain above every surviving nonempty initial token; deleting placements in them removes no support for retained locks and only removes obstacles. The remaining K0 placements constitute a clearing play. The board scan and output length are polynomial.
claims.witness: The reduction maps (B,K0) to survival on B for K0+H floor(W/2) pieces after rejecting the two directly decidable NO conditions.
claims.search_method: Independent saturation/deletion proof and exact clearing-versus-survival equivalence checks for 310 restricted small-board/spawn instances.

target_evidence: The source target requires a full computational-complexity classification for unrestricted finite sequences of unrotatable dominoes. The draft establishes NP membership, several rigorous structural bounds and strategies, counterexamples, and a promise-restricted clearing-to-survival reduction. It supplies neither a polynomial-time algorithm nor an NP-hardness proof for arbitrary starting boards and arbitrary mixed fixed orientations. These results are material but incomplete, exactly matching the draft's PARTIAL resolution claim.
checks_performed: Read only /evidence/source.json and /evidence/parent.json as evidence inputs; used no web or other solution material.
Re-derived the row-token capacity bound, mixed-orientation endpoint-charge inequality, q=0 startup case, and restricted reduction without relying on claimed_resolution or self_assessment.
Created and ran /work/audit_attempt2_exact_checker.py using exact integer row masks, directed translation reachability, fixed-orientation locks, and simultaneous row deletion.

The checker passed 4,628 claim-1 cases; 78,968 mixed-obstruction count-state nodes from 2,353 initial cases; 204 two-cycle sharpness cases; 733 even-width horizontal cycle cases; 253 vertical cycle cases; every stated finite witness; and 310 restricted-reduction equivalence cases.
